anx1d: Revenue, spending, budget path 2028–2047, scenarios, household profiles
anx2d: The code driving the calculator on this page — today against 28:28
anx3d: Transfer to ten countries: dividend rule, cost, ordering
anx4d: Law as of 2026, data basis, and what has not yet been checked
anx_lede: Nothing on this page has to be taken on trust. Every figure comes from the models below — complete, readable, recalculable.
bud_p1: Yes — in all three calculations, without a single year of shortfall. A cushion builds up before the first payment; after that, up to 1 % of GDP a year remains for flexible investment, and a further 2 % stands ready as a crisis reserve.
bud_p2: Even in the recession test the dividend is not cut. Only the annual adjustment pauses; its value then falls temporarily by up to 9 %. The state's existing structural deficit of around 2.7 % of GDP is deliberately outside this calculation — it would have to be closed on top.
calc_calib: Calibration: Germany as the example economy. The logic transfers to other developed countries; the parameters are set per country.
calc_fine: Today: German income tax schedule, solidarity surcharge, contribution rates and ceilings for 2026, child benefit 259 €; the comparison with the child tax allowance is not included. 28:28: contributions of 14 % (9 % from the 617 € step) on the whole gross, tax on gross plus dividend, child dividend tax-free. Consumption label: an effective 20 % instead of around 16.5 %, at a typical consumption ratio. Excluding basic income support, housing benefit and student support — the legacy guarantee covers those.
calc_lede: German law as it stands in 2026 against 28:28 — with exactly the code published below under the models.
calc_r4: Tax and contributions as % of gross
calc_r5: Extra cost from the consumption label (estimated)
cl_e1p: 57 % of the EU population and about 70 % of its output. A group this size sets rules instead of following them — including towards the large platforms. Nine countries would already be enough for that.
cl_e2p: Tørsløv, Wier and Zucman count five tax havens inside the EU: Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Malta and the Netherlands. In 2016 some 117 bn USD of shifted profits flowed to Ireland, 90 bn to the Netherlands and 15 bn to Belgium. Three of the five are on this list; Luxembourg and Malta are not. All three would lose revenue — that calls for transitional compensation out of the other seven countries' additional receipts.
cl_e2t: Three of the five EU tax havens would be inside
cl_e3p: In nine of the ten countries the top income tax rate falls, in Denmark by 32 points. Only Estonia would have to raise it, from 24 to 28 %. With corporate tax it is the other way round: it rises in nine countries — in Ireland by 15.5 points — and falls only in Germany.
cl_e4p: Enhanced cooperation under the EU treaties requires at least nine member states. The club could therefore start inside EU law, without waiting for unanimity among all 27. Ten country files means one country can decline without blocking the route.
cl_e4t: Nine are enough, ten are calculated
cl_e5p: The dividend ranges from 306 € in Estonia to 651 € in Austria; in purchasing power the gap is smaller. Workers enjoy full equal treatment. For arrivals without earnings a waiting period would have to be examined, of the kind Alaska applies to its dividend.
cl_e6p: Because top rates fall across the whole club, it becomes more attractive for high incomes and for new businesses — a counterweight to departures caused by the wealth and inheritance tax.
cl_ee_h3: Why Estonia is in the club
cl_ee_l1: From January 2026 a single rate of 24 % applies to income, to distributed profits and to VAT. That is effectively a 24:24.
cl_ee_l2: Property tax has been based on the value of the land alone since 1993; buildings are untaxed. That is component 04, in operation for over thirty years.
cl_ee_l3: A tax return is filed digitally in minutes — the administrative precondition for component 01.
cl_ee_l4: At 24.1 % Estonia has the lowest debt ratio in the EU: the pilot country with the most room and the least risk.
cl_ee_p: With 1.4 million inhabitants Estonia is the smallest member — and today the closest to the construction principle of 28:28.
cl_ex_p: The same rule applied to ten economies: Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Belgium, Austria, Denmark, Slovenia and Estonia. Together 257.2 million inhabitants — 56.9 % of the EU population — and about 70 % of its output. Enhanced cooperation under the EU treaties requires nine member states, so ten files leave one place to spare. Not all of them have to take part. Slovenia stands for the ordinary case, a mid-sized euro country with no special role; Ireland for the hardest one. Under the single dividend rule, these are the monthly amounts for adults:
cl_g1p: One rate for income, for profits and for the top consumption step. It may glide only by rule, between 25 and 30 % — the corridor within which each country finds its value.
cl_g2p: It is a fixed share of national median income: 21.4 %, derived from the 515 € in Germany. Children receive half. The rule is the same everywhere; the amount follows the country's income level.
cl_g3p: Profits are taxed where the customers are. This is the one component that grows stronger with every new member: the larger the group, the fewer ways around it.
cl_ie_l1: Corporate tax would have to rise from 12.5 to 28 % — the largest single step on the list. Irish corporation tax is also extremely concentrated: the Irish Fiscal Advisory Council reports that in 2024 three groups paid about 46 % of it, roughly 13 bn €.
cl_ie_l2: Irish GDP is inflated by multinational accounting. Measured against modified gross national income, GNI*, which the Irish statistical office publishes for exactly this reason, the dividend costs 10.2 % — the same as in Germany, not the 5.6 % that GDP suggests.
cl_ie_l3: Component 05 does not need Ireland. Tax falls where the sale happens, regardless of where the profit is booked. The component works unilaterally — that is its point. Ireland's accession buys something else: legal peace inside the EU instead of proceedings against a member state.
cl_ie_l4: For the Irish population the arithmetic would be favourable: top rate from 48 to 28 %, a dividend of 626 € a month. What would be lost is a source of state revenue that depends on a few foreign groups — not the prosperity of the people.
cl_ie_p: Ireland is on this list because a design must not hide the winners of the present system. As an early joiner it is at the same time the least likely of the ten.
cl_lede: Germany is only the worked example in this design. The system is built so that the economy is exchangeable: the same rules everywhere, national values everywhere. The aim is to win several countries for a joint start by 2028.
cl_limits: What this calculation does not do: there is no multi-country model. Only the gross cost of the dividend at national income levels is calculated; tariff revenue, corporations, consumption, land, carbon and the contribution reform are not modelled per country. Existing benefits and contribution systems differ widely — Denmark and Estonia finance their welfare states largely out of taxes, so the lever of lowering contributions is largely absent there. Belgium, Ireland and the Netherlands would lose revenue from taxation at the place of the customer, which is not netted off here. Purchasing power differences are not calculated. This becomes defensible only with EUROMOD, which represents all tax and benefit systems on one basis.
cl_t1: The models are published. Experts, administrations and critics are invited to recalculate them and name the errors.
cl_t2: For each interested country the same calculation is filled with national data — verifiable with EUROMOD, the EU's open tax-benefit model.
cl_t3: The earliest realistic year after legislation and administrative build-up. Latecomers follow the same rule set.
cl_t4: Every further country strengthens the effect, above all in taxing profits where the customers are.
cl_tbl_fine: Dividend: 21.4 % of national median equivalised income, children half. Cost: gross cost of the dividend as % of output. ² For Ireland the reference is modified gross national income, GNI*, not GDP: Irish GDP is inflated by multinational accounting, and GNI* is 55.5 % of it. Measured against GDP the figure would be 5.6 %. Notional rate: the German model (28) shifted linearly by the higher or lower cost of the dividend — an ordering, not a national calculation. Sources: GDP and GDP per capita IMF, April 2026 projection, converted at the ECB average rate for 2026; median equivalised income from a WKO compilation of EU-SILC data, as of 2025 (not a primary source, so the values are provisional); top income tax and corporate rates Tax Foundation 2026, Estonia per the Estonian Chamber of Commerce; debt at end-2025 Eurostat, euro indicators of 22 April 2026; Irish GNI* from the Central Statistics Office. The output share compares country projections for 2026 with the EU total for 2025 and is therefore an upper bound.
con_lede: Every element is already proven somewhere in the world — from Estonia's digital administration and land tax to Alaska's dividend. 28:28 assembles them into a load-bearing system.
diag1p: Statutes, regulations, decrees, rulings — almost nobody can see through it without advice.
diag2p: In the British Virgin Islands, 30.2 m USD of profit falls on every employed person, taxed at 2.1 %. In Germany it is 44,345 USD.
diag2t: of corporate profits in tax havens
diag3p: Someone on basic income support who works more often keeps only 10 to 20 cents of each extra euro.
diag4p: AI and automation raise output — the returns concentrate, the tax base of labour erodes.
diag_fine: Orders of magnitude, not point estimates. The page count comes from project research; a solid citation is still missing. Profit shifting after Tørsløv, Wier and Zucman; the ifo Institute, working from the country-by-country reports of large groups, arrives at much lower figures. German rules on earnings while on basic income support, as of 2026. Profit per employed person: own analysis of the OECD country-by-country reports, dataset DSD_CBCR@DF_CBCRI, 2023, sub-groups with positive profit.
diag_h2: Too complex to understand. Too porous to be fair.
diag_lede: And the gains of progress pass us by. Four cracks in today's system:
erb_h3: No exemption, but a fair transition
erb_p1: Today’s relief for business assets works most strongly where the largest fortunes change hands. It is abolished outright. Anyone inheriting a business or a home therefore faces a tax on assets that are not cash.
erb_p2: A deferral takes its place. Interest runs at first at the rate at which the state refinances itself; over ten years it rises to the market lending rate. Only the interest is payable as it falls due. For anyone who cannot carry even that, it is added to the outstanding balance. That balance stays as a charge on the inherited asset and falls due when the asset is sold or passed on.
erb_p3: So nobody has to sell in order to pay the tax – and nobody is given anything. Nothing is written off, nothing can lapse. The deferral stays a deferral.
ev_g1: The 2026 schedule and parameters are documented (§ 32a German Income Tax Act). The revenue is estimated across the income distribution in three scenarios, not computed from primary data. Next step: the official income tax statistics by income bracket.
ev_g10: The 2026 contribution rates and ceilings are documented. That contributions can fall to 28 and later 18 % follows from the overall calculation and is only as sound as that.
ev_g2: The 2026 legal position is documented. The revenue effect rests on a realisation elasticity of 0.7 to 1.0 — an assumption taken from the literature. Next step: the capital income tax statistics.
ev_g3: Own analysis of the official German inheritance and gift tax statistics 2024 (245,540 acquisitions, 113.2 bn €). An inheritance of 150,000 € is taxed at an effective 13.5 %; one of 15 m € at 9.6 % — in that bracket 61.9 % of the acquisition is exempt. The business-asset relief covers 79.4 % of all business assets transferred and costs 3.9 to 5.1 bn € a year. Position 03 would raise 20.98 bn € instead of 13.28, that is +7.7 bn € — computed on an exact class boundary of the official statistics. The exemption is replaced by a deferral: the state loses nothing, the concession is limited to the bank margin of the early years and amounts to about 0.7 bn €.
ev_g4: Not computed. The land value levy lacks a tax base. Next step: the value of land from the sectoral balance sheets.
ev_g5: Own analysis of the OECD country-by-country reports, 2016 to 2023, 63 reporting jurisdictions. Tested with two apportionment keys and on a constant panel of continuously reporting states: for Germany +5 to +14 bn €, median +8. Apportioning by sales alone is a design choice — it makes the rule unilaterally enforceable but works less strongly against tax havens.
ev_g6: The five tiers are set; their weights of 10/10/20/30/30 are assumed. The effective rate of 20 % follows from them. Next step: map consumption expenditure by purpose onto the tiers.
ev_g7: Own calculation on the Third Act amending the German Fuel Emissions Trading Act. § 44(2) fixes the emission volumes to 2030: 301.0 → 180.6 m tonnes, −40 %. § 10(2) sentence 4 sets a price corridor of 55 to 65 € for 2026 and 2027. Revenue from national fuel emissions trading in 2026 is therefore 13.9 to 16.4 bn €. From 2028 the price is set by European emissions trading — a nationally set path is then no longer possible, hence the European wording. The removal of subsidies stays open: of the 65.4 bn € reported by the Federal Environment Agency (data year 2018) about 47 would raise revenue, 12.7 are electricity-price reliefs that never reach the budget — and several items have since lapsed.
ev_g8: Level and indexation are documented: 50 % of the official 2026 subsistence minimum, with steps at 55 and 60 %. The gross cost is computed. Whether it can be carried depends on the other positions.
ev_g9: Not computed. The grandfathering guarantee and the hardship fund require a household microsimulation. That presupposes a data contract for SOEP or EU-SILC.
ev_lede: What each figure rests on, position by position. Four levels: computed from an official source; own calculation with an approximation; computed from distributional assumptions; not computed. Today two rows are substantiated and two are open. Every new calculation moves a row.
ev_leg: ■■■ computed from an official source and reproducible · ■■□ own calculation from an official source, with a design choice or approximation · ■□□ computed from distributional assumptions, no primary data · □□□ not computed.
ev_note: This table is why the proposal can be checked: it also says where the figures are thin. The scripts are in the annex, the calculation steps in the logbook.
ft_i_p: Responsible for content: Initiative 28 : 28 — Arndt Hermann, 2828@archicrowd.de. This page uses no cookies, no trackers and loads no third-party content. No personal data is collected. The fonts Space Grotesk, Source Serif 4 and IBM Plex Mono are served locally under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. All model calculations are illustrations without warranty and do not replace tax or legal advice. The page is excluded from search engines.
ft_m_p: Revenue and budget are recalculated across the income distribution and tested in three ways — optimistic, cautious and with a recession. The uncomfortable figures are on the page too. Developed with the method of architectural design, in a working dialogue with an AI system.
ft_note: German is the original version of this design. The other language versions are translations and have not been checked by a specialist.
hero_h1: The simple tax system for the 21st century.
hero_open: Every calculation model is open source and checkable here.
hero_sub: No more than 28 % on any income — and 28 % for corporations, platforms, heirs and large fortunes too. Plus a digital dividend of 515 € a month for every adult, from day one.
hh_fine: ¹ Today, depending on circumstances, student support, basic income support or no benefit; the legacy guarantee secures the previous level. Inge: today including the minimum pension top-up.
js_less: less a year after the consumption label,
js_more: more a year after the consumption label,
meta_desc: No more than 28 % on any income, 28 % for corporations, platforms, heirs and large fortunes too, plus a digital dividend of 515 € a month. Every model open to inspection.
p01aria: Tax brackets from 0 to 28 per cent
p01p: The base is gross income — no deductions, no joint filing. Subsistence income stays tax-free; above it, work pays at every level.
p01t: Bracket tariff with a hard ceiling
p02p: Realised gains count too. Reclassifying wages as capital income no longer pays.
p03p: One rate, no exemptions. Anyone inheriting a business or a home can defer the tax: initially at the state’s own refinancing rate, rising over ten years to the market lending rate. Nothing is written off – the outstanding balance stays as a charge on the asset and falls due on sale.
p04p: Wealth up to 2 m € is left practically untouched. Property tax follows the value of the plot alone, not the house on it — as it already does in Baden-Württemberg since 2025 and in Estonia since 1993. Building or renovating no longer raises the bill; unused building land in a good location pays. The tax may not be passed on to tenants.
p04r: 1 % above 2 m € · property tax on land only
p04t: Large fortunes and valuable land contribute
p05p: This applies expressly to digital platforms. Profits can be moved; a customer base cannot.
p06aria: VAT label from A plus to D
p06p: As with the energy label, you see at a glance what a product costs — and why. The more sustainable, the cheaper. Effective rate on a standard basket around 20 %.
p07p: From 2028 the carbon price is set by European emissions trading, not by the German parliament. 28:28 therefore sets no national price but calls for a common path along the agreed climate targets – a task for the club. The proceeds come back through the dividend: those who consume little gain. Tax breaks for fossil use end.
p07r: European price path · returned through the dividend
p07t: A carbon price returned to everyone
p08aria: Dividend steps of 515, 566 and 617 euro a month
p08p: For every adult; children receive half. The amount is tied to the official subsistence threshold and rises by formula, not by election promise. It is taxable: at the bottom almost all of it stays, at the top 28 % flows back.
p09p: Anyone on basic income support, minimum pension or student support today receives at least the previous level — the hardship fund pays the difference. It also covers housing costs, care, disability and exceptional circumstances.
p09r: Legacy guarantee · 40 bn € for targeted help
p09t: Nobody on a low income falls behind
p10p: Contributions fall to 28 % at once and to 18 % with the next dividend step. In exchange, high incomes pay on every euro — no exceptions applies in both directions.
p10t: More net from gross — for everyone
r1p: Corporations, platforms, capital, inheritances, large fortunes and land are taxed under the new law several months before the first payment. The dividend starts on a cushion, never on credit.
r2p: The dividend is half the official subsistence threshold. It rises in steps to 60 % as soon as the crisis reserve is full and investment is secured.
r3p: If the reserve is drawn on, only the annual adjustment is suspended. It is made up solely out of surpluses.
r4p: 2 % of GDP stands ready as a crisis reserve; beyond that, up to 1 % of GDP flows every year into schools, networks and railways. The state stays able to act without new debt.
r5b: Fiscal council, open figures, a fixed corridor.
r5p: An independent council audits every assumption annually; the actual figures are public monthly. As a last safeguard, the uniform rate may glide only by rule, between 25 and 30 %.
safe_h2: Why the budget cannot tip over
safe_lede: A design is only as good as its safeguards. Five rules decide — not election campaigns.
sim_fine: Paths from 2028 are model calculations, not forecasts. Debt: the ratio net of the fund reserve. Inequality: a model estimate; only an order of magnitude of 2 to 5 Gini points is defensible. The carbon path is carried over from the earlier version.
sim_lede: Four indicators from 2010 to 2035: the path to today, and from 2028 two futures — business as usual, or with 28:28.
src_text:
ASSUMPTIONS AND SOURCES — TAX 28:28
As of September 2026. This list also names what is not evidenced.

1 | GERMAN LAW 2026 (basis of the calculator)
  Income tax schedule, § 32a EStG 2026, basic allowance 12,348 €
  Solidarity surcharge, exemption threshold 20,350 €
  Contribution rates and ceilings 2026: ceiling for health and
    long-term care insurance 69,750 €, for pension and
    unemployment insurance 101,400 €; employee share of health
    and care insurance 10.55 %, childless surcharge 0.6 %,
    pension and unemployment insurance 10.6 %
  Child benefit 259 € a month
  Average earnings 51,944 €
  Not included: comparison with the child tax allowance,
    church tax, work-related expenses above the standard amount

2 | PARAMETERS OF 28:28
  Bracket tariff 0 / 9 / 16 / 21 / 26 / 28 %
    thresholds 12,348 / 25,000 / 40,000 / 55,000 / 70,000 €
  VAT label 5 / 11 / 17 / 22 / 28 %, effective rate 20.0 %
    weights of the steps 10 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 30 % — ASSUMPTION
  Inheritance: allowance 200,000 € per acquisition, rate 28 %, no
    exemptions. Deferral for businesses and real property: rate in year t
    = refinancing rate + (t-1)/9 x margin, full market rate from year 10.
    No write-off; the balance is a charge on the asset, due on sale.
    Only the interest is payable as it falls due; the balance stays
    a charge on the asset. Present value to the state per 100 EUR:
    102 after five, 108 after ten, 121 after twenty years — no loss,
    and the longer the deferral, the more.
  Carbon: no nationally set price. Volumes under § 44(2) of the Fuel
    Emissions Trading Act (third amending act): 252.4 m t in 2026,
    180.6 m t in 2030. Price corridor under § 10(2) sentence 4: 55 to
    65 EUR for 2026 and 2027. From 2028 a market-based price following
    the EU ETS 1 average (§ 10(3) sentence 2 no. 4); transition into
    ETS 2, whose start Regulation (EU) 2026/667 postponed by a year.
    The price path is therefore a European demand, not a national one.
  Digital dividend 50 % of subsistence income = 515 € a month,
    steps 55 % = 566 € and 60 % = 617 €, children half
  Employee social contributions 14 %, 9 % from the 617 € step
  Crisis reserve 2 % of GDP, flexible investment up to 1 % a year

3 | BEHAVIOURAL RESPONSES (literature)
  Elasticity of taxable income 0.25 / 0.35 / 0.50 by scenario.
    Literature: Doerrenberg, Peichl and Siegloch 0.35 to 0.68;
    Werdt 0.36
  Semi-elasticity of reported profits 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.5;
    meta-analysis Heckemeyer and Overesch about 0.8
  Realisation elasticity for capital gains
    0.7 / 0.8 / 1.0 — ASSUMPTION

4 | EVIDENCE STATUS (in full in the "Evidence status" section)
  Substantiated from an official source:
    Position 03 Inheritance — Federal Statistical Office of Germany,
      inheritance and gift tax statistics 2024, statistical report
      73611, tables 73611-01, -04, -05, -06, -07. 245,540
      acquisitions, 113.2 bn EUR. Revenue at a 200,000 EUR
      allowance and 28 %: 20.98 bn EUR against 13.28 bn today.
    Position 08 Dividend — level and link to the subsistence minimum.
  Order of magnitude with a source:
    Position 05 Corporations — OECD, Corporate Tax Statistics,
      dataset DSD_CBCR@DF_CBCRI (1.1), 2016 to 2023, 63 reporting
      jurisdictions. Own apportionment under four keys, normalised
      on 26 continuously reporting states: +5 to +14 bn EUR,
      median +8. The single-factor key is a design choice.
  Not yet computed:
    Revenue from the land value charge
    Size of the climate-damaging subsidies to be removed. The Federal
      Environment Agency reports 65.4 bn EUR for 2018. Own allocation:
      about 47 bn of that would raise revenue, 12.7 bn are
      electricity-price reliefs with no budget effect, 4.8 bn are
      spending. Several items have since lapsed (EEG levy 2022,
      peak-load compensation 2023). A current edition is missing.
    Weights of the VAT steps
    Page count of tax law (the figure in the diagnosis)
    The share of winners is a model estimate, not a
      microsimulation. A check with GETTSIM or EUROMOD on SOEP
      or EU-SILC microdata is still outstanding.
  Open from the decisions on deferral:
    Transition gap of about 4.5 bn EUR a year over ten years
      (45 bn cumulative) — a pure shift in timing, but it belongs
      in the budget of the early years.
    Compatibility of the interest ladder with § 234 of the German
      Fiscal Code.
    Administrative effort at a 200,000 EUR allowance: the statistics
      do not say how many estates would newly have to be assessed;
      they only cover what reaches the tax office today.
    The assessed tax of 13.28 bn EUR is a gross figure; the
      remissions under the exemption needs test (§ 28a Inheritance
      Tax Act) are not included. The additional revenue is therefore
      understated rather than overstated.

5 | NOT PART OF THIS CALCULATION
  The state's existing structural deficit of around 2.7 % of
  GDP. The reform balances in itself; it does not also repair
  the inherited position.

6 | COUNTRY FILES
  GDP and GDP per capita: IMF, April 2026 projection
  Conversion: ECB average rate 2026, 0.8611 EUR per USD
  Median equivalised income: WKO compilation of EU-SILC
    data, as of 2025 — not a primary source
  Top income tax and corporate rates: Tax Foundation 2026;
    Estonia from January 2026 per the Estonian Chamber of
    Commerce, on distributed profits
  Deficit 2025 and debt at end-2025: Eurostat, euro
    indicators of 22 April 2026
  Ireland: GNI* 334.0 bn EUR against GDP 602.4 bn EUR (2025),
    Central Statistics Office Ireland. For Ireland GNI* is
    the reference measure. Concentration of corporation tax:
    Irish Fiscal Advisory Council, 2024 data.
  Shifted profits and classification as a tax haven:
    Tørsløv, Wier and Zucman, updated figures 2019 (2016
    data). Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Malta and the
    Netherlands are counted there as EU tax havens.
  Share aged 0 to 14: World Bank; Estonia, Ireland, Belgium
    and Slovenia estimated
  Estonian land tax: Estonian Tax and Customs Board
stamp1: Dividend per month from day one — 257.50 € per child
stamp2: of people have more in their pocket
stamp3: disposable income for a family with two children
stamp_note: * Estimated from the model, not a microsimulation. Without the legacy guarantee, around 5 % would be worse off, mainly households on basic income support without earnings. With the legacy guarantee (component 09), a loss affects only parts of very large fortunes.
